record.title: A study finds LLM aggregators can treat repeated reports as partly independent evidence
record.summary: Gao and colleagues study how four language models count repeated reports across controlled sensor logs with an exact Bayesian oracle, web documents, and generated multi-agent transcripts. Their abstract reports that a forwarded copy counts as 0.06–0.42 of an independent reading, and that repeated statements can imply premature commitment on 5%–40% of logs in the tested settings. The authors report that a declaration about copy contribution lowers copy weight to 0.08 or less on controlled logs, while a worker-side rule to refer to readings rather than restate them lowers belief-implied early commitment from 11.2% to 1.1% in their team-log protocol. This is one author-reported preprint, not an operational error rate or independent replication.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_PUBLICATION_EVENT
claims.text: The authors published a study of how language-model aggregators interpret repeated evidence across three testbeds and four models.

claims.label: CLAIMED_BY_AUTHORS
claims.text: Across the tested models, a forwarded copy counted as 0.06–0.42 of a new reading; on 5%–40% of logs with one reading stated three times, reported beliefs implied early commitment that the oracle did not make.

claims.label: CLAIMED_BY_AUTHORS
claims.text: A worker instruction to refer to readings rather than restate them reduced belief-implied early commitment from 11.2% to 1.1% in the authors’ generated team-log protocol.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The study does not establish deployed multi-agent error rates or independent replication of its results.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent replication or operational multi-agent evaluation was identified in this activation.
This activation re-read the abstract, not the current full-text version, public data, or implementation.
The abstract reports a worker-side reference rule but does not fully expose how results vary across communication protocols or incomplete relay logs.

brief.importance_rationale: If an aggregator gives repeated statements nonzero evidential weight, multi-agent workflows can become overconfident without receiving new information. The study reports controlled, synthetic and author-generated effects plus mitigations; transfer to operational systems remains uncertain.
limitations: Evidence is author-reported in one preprint and has not been independently reproduced.
Testbeds include controlled synthetic logs, web-document copies and author-generated team logs; they do not establish a deployed-system error rate.
Reported early-commitment effects depend on the tested models, prompts, protocol and oracle assumptions.
The abstract does not establish transfer to naturally occurring source-provenance graphs or broader agent tasks.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report a 0.06–0.42 copy weight, premature commitment on 5%–40% of selected repeated-report logs, and a worker reference-rule reduction from 11.2% to 1.1% in one protocol.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint and its abstract are public; measured outcomes are author-reported.
technical.implementation_status: Research study; no deployed-system intervention was evaluated.
technical.mechanism: The authors vary how one fixed observation is restated and translate reported model probabilities into units of independent readings; they also test declarations and worker instructions to refer to evidence rather than repeat it.
technical.novelty: Measures whether an aggregator treats repeated statements as partially new evidence and tests source-reference interventions.
technical.regime: Four models from three providers across three testbeds: controlled sensor logs with an exact Bayesian oracle, web documents with appended copies, and generated multi-agent communication logs.
technical.reproducibility: No independent replication in this activation. Candidate memory reports limited within-paper repeat-sample stability, not independent reproduction.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched cases holding the underlying evidence fixed while varying restatement or independent readings; an exact Bayesian oracle is used for controlled logs.

brief.title: A study finds LLM aggregators can treat repeated reports as partly independent evidence
brief.why_it_matters: Multi-agent systems can relay the same observation through summaries, boards and discussion rounds. If an aggregator partly counts each restatement as a new source, confidence may rise without new evidence. The findings support explicit source ancestry and separate tests of worker communication and aggregator reasoning, while leaving real-world rates and cross-domain transfer unresolved.
